events.title: United States Pays Off the National Debt
events.description: On January 8, 1835, under President Andrew Jackson, the United States national debt was reduced to zero for the only time in its history, following years of federal surpluses from land sales and tariff revenue.
events.significance: It remains the sole occasion on which the U.S. government was completely debt-free, and it is frequently cited in debates about fiscal policy.

events.title: Battle of New Orleans
events.description: On January 8, 1815, American forces under General Andrew Jackson decisively defeated a larger British army led by Sir Edward Pakenham near New Orleans, Louisiana. The battle was fought after the Treaty of Ghent had been signed but before news reached North America.
events.significance: The victory made Jackson a national hero, boosted American national pride at the end of the War of 1812, and helped propel him toward the presidency.

events.title: Birth and Death Milestones: Stephen Hawking Born; Galileo Died
events.description: Stephen Hawking, the English theoretical physicist, was born on January 8, 1942, exactly 300 years after the death of Galileo Galilei, who died on January 8, 1642, at Arcetri, Italy.
events.significance: Galileo's work laid the foundations of modern observational astronomy and physics, while Hawking advanced understanding of black holes, cosmology, and the popularization of science. The coincidence of dates is often noted in the history of science.

events.title: Fidel Castro Enters Havana
events.description: On January 8, 1959, Fidel Castro and his rebel forces arrived triumphantly in Havana, Cuba, days after dictator Fulgencio Batista fled the country on January 1.
events.significance: The event marked the consolidation of the Cuban Revolution and the start of a communist government in Cuba that reshaped Cold War geopolitics in the Western Hemisphere.

events.title: Moscow Metro Bombings
events.description: On January 8, 1977, three bombs exploded in Moscow, including in a subway train and near stores, killing seven people. Soviet authorities later executed three Armenian men for the attacks.
events.significance: The bombings were among the first major terrorist attacks in the Soviet capital, challenging official claims of domestic security and drawing controversy over the fairness of the trial.
